summary: Describes how to carry IPv6 over Power Line Communication networks, which use electric power lines for data, widely used for smart meters. It specifies an adaptation layer based on 6LoWPAN-style techniques so constrained devices can use IPv6 over these links.

eli5.summary: Wires that bring electricity can also carry messages. This explains how to make the internet's newer address system work over them, for things like smart meters.

questions: how do smart meters use ipv6
how does ipv6 work over plc
how are plc interface identifiers formed
subtitle: How to run IPv6 over the electric power lines that connect smart meters and street lights.

tldr.problem: Power Line Communication (PLC) links carry data for smart meters and similar devices, but the 6LoWPAN adaptation layer alone does not fit PLC media, and the devices are constrained in power, memory and processing.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adapts 6LoWPAN and 6lo techniques for PLC: IIDs built from long or short link-layer addresses, link-local addresses, address options for the 12-bit and 16-bit short addresses, 6LoWPAN neighbor discovery, RFC 6282 header compression and RFC 4944 fragmentation.
tldr.outcome: It covers IEEE 1901.1, IEEE 1901.2 and ITU-T G.9903 networks, so constrained PLC devices can use IPv6 over star, tree and mesh topologies.

today: RFC 9354 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2023. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: IPv6 on the Power Grid
sections.content:
Power Line Communication (PLC) uses electric power lines for communication. It has been widely applied to Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), especially smart meters. The devices in these scenarios share common features: fixed position, a large number of nodes, low data rate and low power consumption.

RFC 9354 describes how IPv6 packets are transported over constrained PLC networks such as those described in ITU-T G.9903, IEEE 1901.1 and IEEE 1901.2. The general approach is to adapt elements of the 6LoWPAN and 6lo specifications (RFC 4944, RFC 6282, RFC 6775 and RFC 8505) to constrained PLC networks.
sections.eli5: Electricity meters sit all over a town, joined by the same wires that bring power. This RFC teaches them to speak the newer internet language over those wires.

sections.title: PLC Technologies, Addresses and MTU
sections.content:
PLC is split into Narrowband PLC (NBPLC, for sensor automation) and Broadband PLC (BBPLC, for home and industry networking). This specification focuses on IEEE 1901.1, IEEE 1901.2 and ITU-T G.9903. The stack is the usual one, with an adaptation layer for IPv6 over PLC sitting between the IPv6 layer and the PLC MAC and PHY layers.

Each PLC device has a globally unique long address (48 bits for IEEE 1901.1, 64 bits for IEEE 1901.2 and ITU-T G.9903) and a short address (12 bits for IEEE 1901.1, 16 bits for the other two). A device joins using its long address and then communicates using its short address.

IPv6 requires an MTU of 1280 octets or greater. The IEEE 1901.1 MAC supports upper-layer packets up to 2031 octets, IEEE 1901.2 supports an MTU of 1576 octets, and ITU-T G.9903 has an MTU of 400 octets. Even where the MAC MTU is large enough, an operator may configure a smaller one in a noisy environment, so the 6lo functions stay useful.
sections.eli5: Every device has a long name used to join and a short nickname used afterwards. Some wires can carry big parcels and some only small ones, so big messages sometimes need to be cut up.

sections.title: Interface Identifiers and Link-Local Addresses
sections.content:
A PLC device uses stateless address autoconfiguration to get an IPv6 Interface Identifier (IID), based on either its long or short link-layer address. A 48-bit MAC address MUST first be extended to a 64-bit IID by inserting 0xFFFE as specified in RFC 2464, and the U/L bit is then inverted.

For IEEE 1901.2 and ITU-T G.9903, a 48-bit pseudo-address is formed from the 16-bit PAN ID, 16 zero bits and the 16-bit short address. The IID MUST be derived as 16_bit_PAN:00FF:FE00:16_bit_short_address. For IEEE 1901.1 the pseudo-address is a 24-bit NID, 12 zero bits and a 12-bit TEI, giving YYYY:YYFF:FE00:0XXX.

For privacy, the IID derived from the MAC address SHOULD only be used for link-local address configuration. A PLC host SHOULD use the IID derived from the short address for communication with the public network. By default the hash algorithm SHOULD be SHA256 over the version number, the PAN ID or NID and the short address, truncated to the high 64 bits. The link-local address is the IID appended to the prefix FE80::/64.
sections.eli5: A device builds its internet name from its network nickname. For talking to the outside world it scrambles the nickname so strangers cannot work out which gadget it is.

sections.title: Unicast Address Mapping Options
sections.content:
Address resolution follows Section 7.2 of RFC 4861. RFC 6775 improves it by avoiding multicast Neighbor Solicitations, and RFC 8505 improves the registration procedure further.

This RFC defines the form of the Source Link-Layer Address and Target Link-Layer Address options used in Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement messages. Type is 1 for Source and 2 for Target. Length is 1, in units of 8 octets.

For IEEE 1901.1 the option carries a 24-bit NID, 12 bits of zero padding and a 12-bit TEI. For IEEE 1901.2 and ITU-T G.9903 it carries a 16-bit PAN ID, 16 bits of zero padding and a 16-bit short address.
sections.eli5: When one device asks where another lives, the answer is a little card holding the network number and the nickname, padded out to a fixed size.

sections.title: Neighbor Discovery, Compression and Fragmentation
sections.content:
Neighbor discovery follows RFC 6775 and RFC 8505. Sleeping mode SHOULD still be used for power saving even though PLC devices are electrically powered. For context information, Router Advertisements MUST be used, and the 6LoWPAN context option (6CO) MUST be included. In route-over mode a PLC device MUST register its addresses by sending a unicast link-local NS to the 6LR. Duplicate Address Detection SHOULD NOT be used if DHCPv6 assigns the address or if the address is derived from the unique long or short link-layer address.

Header compression is based on RFC 6282. IEEE 1901.1 needs one change because its short address has 12 bits instead of 16: the meaning of the Source and Destination Address Mode value 10 is adapted so the inline 16 bits have their first 4 bits as zero.

If the configured MAC MTU is below 1280 octets, fragmentation and reassembly from RFC 4944 MUST be used. For ITU-T G.9903, where the maximum MAC payload is fixed at 400 octets, this MUST be provided. The 16-bit datagram tag is judged sufficient because PLC data rates are low.
sections.eli5: Devices sign in with a nearby helper, shorten their long addresses to save space, and cut large messages into small pieces that fit the wire.

sections.title: Topologies and Operations
sections.content:
A PLC network has two kinds of device: the PAN Coordinator (PANC), the primary coordinator of the subnet, and ordinary PLC devices such as meters and sensors. Generally each network has one PANC.

  • Star: common today, with communication only between a device and the PANC, which uploads data over Ethernet or cellular networks. Widely used for smart meters in apartment buildings.
  • Tree: used when a device is too far from the PANC and another device in between acts as a Coordinator. Suited to smart street lighting and rural AMI. RPL suits maintaining a tree.
  • Mesh: nodes connect with all neighbors in range. A smart home is the simple use case, and AODV-RPL enables direct device-to-device communication.

These networks are designed to be self-organized and self-managed. A device that goes offline returns to bootstrapping and tries to rejoin, and the PANC can show onboarding status and topology.
sections.eli5: Meters can talk to one boss in a star, pass messages along a chain like a tree, or talk to any neighbor like friends in a crowd.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
Because power grids are so accessible, PLC might be susceptible to eavesdropping. The RFC gives the example of one apartment tenant monitoring other smart meters in the building. Malicious devices could also disrupt the network by repeatedly joining and leaving or by sending fake routing metrics. Since outside traffic goes through the PANC, the PANC must be a trusted entity, and mutual authentication of network and new device is important during onboarding.

No specific mechanism is mandated, because the right one depends on the deployment. Examples named include the TLS/DTLS profile (RFC 7925), the Constrained Join Protocol (RFC 9031) and EAP methods such as RFC 9140. Where physical attacks are fairly likely, per-device credentials SHOULD be used.

For privacy, globally unique and unchanging address characteristics should be avoided. Schemes such as DHCPv6 lease limits, CGAs, temporary addresses, hash-based addresses or semantically opaque addresses SHOULD be used to improve IID privacy. There are no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: Wires can be listened to, so devices should check who they are talking to and not shout out their real name.
